candidates.summary: Duplicate declarations are still accepted silently by `gno run <dir>` with no -pkgpath; the new RedeclarationErrors branch is only reachable under a non-stdlib-looking path
candidates.failure_scenario: Two files a.gno and b.gno in one directory both declare `func helper()`; with no gnomod.toml and no -pkgpath the package path defaults to the package name "main", gno.IsStdlib("main") is true, so Machine.RunFiles (machine.go:646) calls runFileDecls with withOverrides=true and checkDuplicates never runs. `gno run dir/` prints b.gno's result `2` and exits 0, at head and at the merge base. The PR's own duplicate-declaration test only reaches the new branch because it passes `-pkgpath example.com/main`. A user running a plain directory gets the wrong helper with exit 0 instead of the redeclaration error the PR advertises. Predates the diff; in scope as a missed member of the duplicate-declaration class the diff sweeps.
candidates.verify_by: go test ./gnovm/cmd/gno -run TestRunDefaultPkgPathDuplicateDecl -count=1 with tests/solo-finder-2-default-pkgpath-dup_test.go copied into gnovm/cmd/gno: CURRENT expectation stdout "2\n" passes; the FIXED expectation (stderr redeclarations, exit code 1) fails. Same fixture by hand with the base binary prints 2, rc 0.
candidates.evidence: head test: `--- PASS: TestRunDefaultPkgPathDuplicateDecl` with stdout `2`. Binaries: `[gno-head c1 dir (default pkgpath)] 2 rc=0`, `[gno-base ...] 2 rc=0`; with `-pkgpath example.com/main` head prints `running package "example.com/main": redeclarations for identifiers: "helper" (code=gnoPreprocessError)`.

candidates.summary: A PreprocessError whose message carries no location prints the fabricated location `.:0` instead of none, dropping the importing file the old panic's preprocess stack named
candidates.failure_scenario: main.gno imports an examples package (gno.land/p/zz/dup) whose two files both declare Helper. The duplicate panics as a wrapped error inside the importing file's predefine; doRecover wraps it with tm2 errors.Wrap, whose %v prints only the cause, so Unwrap().Error() has no location, ReErrorLine misses, and guessIssueFromError(".", ".", ...) falls back to Location `.:0`. Head prints `.:0: running package "gno.land/p/zz/dup": redeclarations for identifiers: "Helper" (code=gnoPreprocessError)`; the base panic's stack named `file main/zz/cases2/i1/main.gno:1:1-7:2`. An editor or matcher parsing file:line jumps to `.` line 0. The doc comment promises no location when none is known.
candidates.verify_by: GNOROOT=<tree with examples/gno.land/p/zz/dup a.gno+b.gno duplicating Helper> gno run dir/ where dir/main.gno imports it: head stderr starts with `.:0:`; base stderr contains `stack 1: file main/<dir>/main.gno`
candidates.evidence: [gno-head rc=1] .:0: running package "gno.land/p/zz/dup": redeclarations for identifiers: "Helper" (code=gnoPreprocessError); base: `stack 1: file main/zz/cases2/i1/main.gno:1:1-7:2`

candidates.summary: The guessIssueFromError rewrite also changes `gno lint` and `gno test` output, and no txtar pins either surface
candidates.failure_scenario: guessIssueFromError serves printError for lint and test too. A package with `go f()` linted at base prints `main.gno:main.gno:6:2: goroutines are not permitted (code=gnoUnknownError)`, at head `main.gno:6:2: ...`. No file under gnovm/cmd/gno/testdata mentions gnoPreprocessError or gnoUnknownError, so a later regression of the lint location goes unseen; only the run cases pin the helper.
candidates.verify_by: grep -rh 'gnoPreprocessError\|gnoUnknownError' --include='*.txtar' gnovm returns nothing; add a lint txtar with `go f()` expecting `main.gno:6:2: goroutines are not permitted (code=gnoUnknownError)` and confirm it fails with the common.go hunk reverted
candidates.evidence: grep over every *.txtar: no hit. Binaries: `[gno-base lint c19_go] main.gno:main.gno:6:2: goroutines are not permitted (code=gnoUnknownError)` vs `[gno-head lint c19_go] main.gno:6:2: goroutines are not permitted (code=gnoUnknownError)`
